title: Declare degradation governance and weighted failover matrix for per-model endpoints
creator: Leah Mendoza
description: Create an operational governance document and implementation plan that defines per-endpoint/model SLIs, an error-budget policy, and a weighted multi-region failover and degradation matrix. This ticket covers the decisioning and config surface for: SLI calculation windows, mapping of quality vs latency SLIs, per-variant and per-tenant weightings for failover, adaptive circuit-breaker thresholds, and prioritized load-shedding rules for graceful degradation. The goal is to enable predictable automated failover while preserving revenue-critical routes and giving operators clear remediation levers.
background: We currently have SLI/SLO artifacts but no single authoritative governance that ties per-model quality metrics to concrete error-budget actions across regions. Recent incidents showed inconsistent failover behavior: large tenants were evicted before low-latency but high-value routes, and circuit breakers tripped globally instead of regionally. This work consolidates rules, encodes priority tiers, and produces a config schema the runtime can consume.
proposal: Define canonical SLI set for text generation endpoints: success_rate (semantic-match), p95_latency_ms, token_throughput, and model_quality_regression_rate (weekly).
Standardize SLO windows: 1h (operational), 24h (short-term), 30d (contractual). Error-budget burn computed per-window with burn-rate alerting.
Introduce three degradation tiers: T1 (preserve high-value, low-latency routes), T2 (best-effort routes, degrade model variant), T3 (background or non-customer-facing workloads).
Weighted failover matrix: per-endpoint weight = (route_tier_score * tenant_priority + model_variant_stability_score). Use weights to score candidate regions/variants during failover and evictions.

Circuit-breaker policy: region-local thresholds first (p95 latency > threshold OR error_rate spike), then global escalation after sustained regional burn. Thresholds are quantile-based and adaptive to baseline traffic patterns.
Load-shedding rules: implement prefix-aware KV cache preservation, graceful prefix rejection, and token-budgeted shedding for long sequences. Eviction decisions should prefer T3 then T2 then T1.
Operational hooks: automatic creation of templated postmortems when error-budget breaches occur and automatic canary rollback triggers for model rollouts if quality_regression_rate > X%.
Expose a config schema (YAML) that maps endpoint -> tier -> weight -> circuit-breaker-params -> failover-preferences, to be consumed by routing/orchestration layer.
Provide migration plan for existing endpoints and a compatibility shim so older configs continue to work for one release cycle.
tasks: Draft governance doc and YAML schema
Sync with PM and Design for tier definitions and tenant priority model
Implement validation code in routing service to read YAML and compute weights
Add per-region circuit-breaker implementation and unit tests
Instrument additional SLIs (model_quality_regression_rate) and wire to dashboards
Create burn-rate alert rules and on-call playbook
Run staged rollout on non-production clusters and measure behavior
Perform canary with two mid-sized tenants and gather feedback
Ship config migration tool and deprecation warnings
acceptance_criteria: A canonical governance doc exists in Confluence with explicit SLI definitions and SLO windows
YAML config schema validated by routing service and linted in CI
Routing service computes weighted failover decisions in staging and matches expected priorities in test harness
Regional circuit-breakers operate independently and escalate to global only after configured grace windows
Burn-rate alerts fire at the configured thresholds and create issue templates automatically
Observed degradation during load test follows T3->T2->T1 ordering with KV-preservation behavior
Migration tool converts at least 95% of existing endpoint configs without human edits
PM and on-call lead have signed off and runbooks updated
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive shedding reduces token-costs but may harm perception for some customers; therefore we prioritize tenant + route weight over pure cost metrics.
Decision log: prefer quantile-adaptive thresholds over fixed thresholds to handle multi-tenant bursty traffic.
Open question: how to map business tiering to tenant_priority for multi-tenant orgs with mixed internal routes. PM to propose mapping by 2026-03-08.
Fallback plan: if weighted failover produces regressions, allow operators to opt-out tenants from automated eviction for one-week windows via admin flag.
This ticket intentionally avoids prescribing exact numeric SLO targets; numerical targets will be set per-service in follow-up tickets after measuring baseline.
